items.headline: Macron calls for 'calm and order' after riots across France
items.blurb: French President Emmanuel Macron gives a national address after widespread disorder and as some looting continued in Paris.
items.text: French President Emmanuel Macron has called for "calm and order" after a major day of protests turned into rioting and looting on Saturday, and as some disorder continued in Paris on Sunday. In a national address from the Élysée Palace, he warned those who had taken part not to "escalate", adding: "We all feel anger and shame." Some 550,000 demonstrators took to the streets for largely peaceful protests against rising fuel prices, the cost of living and deteriorating public services, including schools. Macron said a distinction must be drawn between the "legitimate demands" of protesters and "those who destroyed, smashed and looted". The French president said "nothing justifies" the "unbridled" violence seen and said those involved would face justice. Groups of rioters, some dressed in black and wearing masks and balaclavas, also came out in Paris, Marseille and other towns and cities, with some setting fire to cars and buildings. On Sunday, looting and clashes with police continued on a smaller scale in parts of the capital and Lyon. Tear gas and stun grenades were fired at hundreds of people

items.headline: Kenya confirms eighth Ebola case amid widening regional outbreak
items.blurb: Kenyan health authorities say latest patient was likely exposed to the country's first Ebola case.
items.text: Kenyan health authorities say an eighth Ebola case has been detected, bringing the total number of known infections in the East African nation to eight. Director-General for Health Patrick Amoth told Kenya’s Citizen TV that of the 38 people tested on Sunday, one had returned a positive result. “He is a 49-year-old man who is not a healthcare worker. He developed fever, headache and muscle pain,” he said. Amoth said the man, who worked as a patient attendant cleaning utensils and linens, was likely exposed to Kenya’s first Ebola case, discovered earlier this month. He developed symptoms on Saturday, was quarantined and tested for the virus, a Ministry of Health source said. The ministry reported four new cases on Saturday , three of whom were health workers who treated the country’s first Ebola patient, a man who travelled from the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) to Nairobi and died at a Nairobi hospital on October 5. items.text: Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds F or the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on. His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba. “Even my mother calls me Shang now,” the 32-year-old, born Tobi Michael Adeyeye, said in an interview near the university’s lagoon waterfront, where he once emceed gatherings. items.headline: 'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
items.blurb: A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests
items.text: A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests on Saturday. Dramatic footage shared online shows the 19th-century building engulfed in flames, with the spire of its clock tower later collapsing. On Sunday, stunned residents watched as firefighters, who had battled the blaze through the night, assessed the building's structural integrity. Officials have not yet confirmed whether the town hall is at risk of collapse. "Damaging heritage buildings because you're angry with the government is selfish", one resident told the BBC.

items.headline: Kinship and surveillance: The return of Somali piracy
items.blurb: Somalia’s piracy crackdown leaves coastal fishermen struggling to survive.
items.text: Mogadishu, Somalia – The fishing town of Bander Beyla, on Somalia’s Puntland coast, has become a focal point of the renewed piracy crisis. But beyond the hijackings and international security operations, residents are struggling to protect their livelihoods as fishing restrictions, arrests and surveillance reshape daily life. Abdifatah Mohamed has spent 20 years fishing off Somalia’s coast. He began at 15, but says declining catches and foreign trawlers have made it increasingly difficult to support his family. “I don’t catch as much fish anymore, and the prospects for catching lobsters have become rare,” the 35-year-old said. Somalia’s central government collapsed in 1991, weakening maritime oversight and leaving its waters vulnerable to illegal fishing. Some fishermen, angered by foreign vessels exploiting the country’s resources, have turned to piracy. “We’re fishermen no match for the foreign trawlers, who possess capabilities far greater than us, which impacts the livelihoods of our families on land,” Mohamed said. items.text: A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king. Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter. But while Victoria took a genuine interest in Bonetta’s welfare, making the orphan a royal protege and meeting with her over the years, their relationship was part of a bigger agenda. Now, as a biography is published – Becoming Sarah Forbes Bonetta: A Yorùbá Woman in Queen Victoria’s Court – Randle has spoken of his family history. “I don’t think a human being, who has agency, could be ‘gifted’ from one to another, but had she not been gifted to Queen Victoria, would I be here today?” said Randle, a British-Nigerian barrister from London. items.headline: Major fire at Canada military base leaves four dead, dozens injured
items.blurb: Prime Minister Carney said military and emergency crews fought the flames throughout the night in "some of the worst conditions imaginable".
items.text: Four members of the Canadian military have died and dozens were injured in a major fire at a base in the province of Alberta. Addressing the nation on Sunday from Ottawa, Prime Minister Mark Carney described it as "one of the worst tragedies for the forces on Canadian soil in peacetime". The fire broke out at about 16:00 local time (22:00 GMT) on Saturday at Canadian Forces Base Wainwright, one of the country's busiest military training bases, and is now contained. Its cause is still unclear, but officials said it did not appear tied to "terrorist activity". "The nation is in mourning for those brave members of our armed forces who we have lost," said Carney. The BBC has confirmed that Sgt Morgan Wong, Pte Shaun Farrell, Pte Aidan Goulding and Pte Hayden Lykkemark have died. Of the 39 injured people being cared for in hospital, at least 19 are in a critical condition, Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said at a press briefing on Sunday evening. items.headline: Flight from Israel makes emergency landing in Bulgaria after bomb threat
items.blurb: Crew of Austrian Airlines flight OS82 decides to land in Sofia after receiving bomb threat, Bulgarian authorities say.
items.text: An Airbus A320 flight from Tel Aviv to Vienna has made an emergency landing in Bulgaria following a reported bomb threat, according to the Bulgarian Ministry of Transport. Austrian Airlines flight OS82 was near the border with Romania when the crew received a bomb threat and decided to land in the Bulgarian capital, Sofia, the Transport Ministry said in a statement on Sunday. Bulgaria’s Ministry of Defence said an air force MiG-29 fighter jet escorted the plane to Sofia airport. Initial information showed the aircraft carried six crew members and 51 passengers, all of whom have all since disembarked, according to the Transport Ministry’s statement. The airline told the AFP news agency that a security search of the aircraft was conducted. “Once the search of the aircraft is complete, the passengers will be rebooked onto alternative flights as quickly as possible,” the airline said. A crisis response team has been set up, and relevant authorities have launched an investigation into the incident, the Bulgarian Transport Ministry said. items.headline: LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested
items.blurb: At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report .
items.text: At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a new report . More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, according to HIV Justice Network , an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status. The intensifying crackdown comes as the law criminalising homosexuality in the country was toughened earlier this year. On 11 March, Senegal’s parliament amended the penal code, doubling the maximum prison term for consensual same-sex relations to 10 years. The new law introduced penalties of up to seven years in prison and a fine of 500,000 to 5m CFA francs (£650–£6,500) for promoting homosexuality, or supporting or financing LGBTQ+ people and organisations. items.headline: Trump says suspension of Russia sanctions is to keep peace negotiations going
items.blurb: The US president blocked numerous sanctions on Russia two days before they were due to take effect.
items.text: US President Donald Trump has said his decision to suspend several Russian sanctions is an effort to keep Moscow at the negotiating table. "I am in the process of negotiating Peace in the war between Russia and Ukraine," Trump said on his Truth Social messaging platform, adding that he didn't want to "do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table". Trump blocked numerous sanctions on Russia on Friday night, two days before they were due to take effect, as a row with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky deepened. Zelensky told NBC News on Sunday that siding with Russian President Vladimir Putin would be a "historic mistake". Russian envoy Kirill Dmitriev has responded to Trump's order by calling it "an important and truly historic moment". He said the sanctions, which were passed by the US Congress and signed into law by the US president in September, would have inflicted "serious damage" on the US and global market. items.headline: Temple development works worth ₹2,500 crore under way across Telangana: Bhatti Vikramarka
items.text: The State government is spending around ₹2,000 crore on developing temples along the Godavari and riverbank areas ahead of the Godavari Pushkaralu scheduled for next year, Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka said on Sunday. He said ₹276 crore had been allocated for the development of Sri Sitaramachandra Swamy temple at Bhadrachalam and ₹354 crore for the Sri Gnana Saraswati temple at Basar. In all, temple development works were being undertaken across the State at an estimated cost of ₹2,500 crore, he added. Mr. Vikramarka was speaking after laying the foundation stone for a road at an estimated cost of ₹44 crore at Nacharam village in Enkoor mandal of Khammam district. He also offered prayers at the Adbhutha Venkateswara Swamy temple in the village. He said the road would ensure easier access for devotees and create employment and livelihood opportunities for local youth. Highlighting the Congress government’s welfare initiatives, he said fine rice was being distributed to 1.06 crore families, while Rajiv Aarogyasri provided free medical treatment of up to ₹10 lakh per family. items.blurb: Police cited CJP leader Abhijeet Dipke’s reported remarks at the airport on Sunday that the party will strategise its next course of action
items.text: Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders spent nearly five hours waiting at Mandir Marg police station on Sunday for a hearing on the release of party convenors Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, who have been in judicial custody since October 14. The proceedings, however, lasted barely eight to ten minutes before the special executive magistrate (SEM) hearing the matter, citing threats and mental harassment, leaving the duo’s release unresolved for the fifth consecutive day. According to CJP representatives, the SEM arrived at the police station around 1.30pm-2pm but the hearing began only around 5pm. The party alleged that despite submitting surety bonds repeatedly since October 15 and completing the required formalities, its members were being made to wait as fresh objections were raised at different stages. During the hearing, police alleged that CJP leaders Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were planning another protest. Police cited Dipke’s reported remarks at the airport on Sunday that the party will strategise its next course of action. items.blurb: Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal says that at all Muslim organisations have been given representation in the board and those left out could be considered for membership in other bodies
items.text: Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) State president Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal on Sunday downplayed the controversy over the reconstitution of the State Waqf Board. He told the media here that those who had grievances were free to approach the court. Mr. Thangal maintained that all Muslim organisations had been given representation in the board and those left out could be considered for membership in other bodies. “The bodies such as the Hajj Committee and the Madrasa Welfare Fund Board are yet to be reconstituted by the government. Those who have not been included in the Waqf board will be considered for such bodies,” Mr. Thangal said. His comments come against the backdrop of the criticism from the Samastha Kerala Jamiyyathul Ulama faction led by Sunni scholar Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliar that they had not been given fair representation in the board. items.headline: 5 injured in 2 separate gunfire incidents in Manipur; 2 villages targeted by arson by armed militants
items.blurb: Police reported no casualties from the arson and said they had yet to reach the villages near the Indo-Myanmar border.
items.text: Five people sustained injuries in two separate gunfire incidents in Manipur even as unidentified armed miscreants set houses in two villages ablaze, officials said on Sunday. According to police, hours after a 36-year-old man belonging to Kuki community was killed and four others sustained injuries on Saturday, unidentified armed miscreants launched the attack on Tangkhul Naga village in Kamjong district. During the retaliatory attack three people belonging to Tangkhul Naga community sustained injuries. The injured were immediately stabilised at Kamjong Hospital, officials said. In the second incident, a Nepalese couple sustained minor bullet injuries on Sunday around 11.45 am in an ambush carried out by unknown armed miscreants in between Mahadev and Guwaltabi village along National Highway 202 (Imphal-Nagaland via Ukhrul) road, police said. According to police, the injured have been identified as one Sandip Dahal (35) and his wife Bepanah Dahal (29) from Charhajare, Kangpokpi district. Officials said both sustained minor bullet injuries below their knees and both of them were discharged from a nearby Army hospital after they were given first aid. items.headline: Elaborate arrangements made for Teppotsavam in Vijayawada on October 20
items.blurb: Police personnel and expert swimmers deployed at bathing ghats along the Krishna River; the float festival was cancelled in 2025 and 2024 due to floods
items.text: Hamsa Vahanam, a swan-shaped boat, being readied for the Teppotsavam at Durga Ghat along the Krishna River in Vijayawada. | Photo Credit: G.N. RAO Elaborate arrangements are being made for the Teppotsavam (float festival), the concluding ceremony of the nine-day Dasara Navaratri celebrations of the Kanaka Durga temple atop Indrakeeldari in Vijayawada, in the Krishna River on October 20. Devotees are excited for the Teppotsavam this year as it was cancelled in the last two years due to the floods in the Krishna. Officials of endowments, police, irrigation and other departments are making elaborate arrangements for the boat ride of Goddess Kanaka Durga and Lord Malleswara Swamy. The Hamsa Vahanam, on which the deities will take a ride on the Krishna river, has been decked up. The officials conducted a trial run of the Hamsa Vahanam (boat) on Sunday. The police have deployed personnel on the ghats as a precautionary measure and the Irrigation Department has deployed expert swimmers at the bathing ghats. items.blurb: Three motorcycle-borne men had opened fire at Shroff in Juhu area of Mumbai on Sunday evening. The actor escaped unhurt, while three others were injured.
items.text: After the attack bid on Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff, two members of the Lawrence Bishnoi gang – Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu – are now under the scanner of police and law enforcement agencies. Three motorcycle-borne men had opened fire at Shroff in Juhu area of Mumbai on Sunday evening. While the actor escaped unhurt, three people, including his driver and an autorickshaw driver, were injured in the incident, according to police. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed the attack , with gangster Anil Pandit saying Harman Sandhu and him were behind the shooting incident. Both Pandit and Sandhu have been accused of orchestrating attacks in Delhi and Punjab, with sources in the Mumbai Police saying they were trying to rise up in rank within the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, HT reported earlier. Among these attacks is an incident in June, wherein alleged gang members opened fire at a gym in west Delhi. items.headline: Ahead of IPO, AI firm Anthropic announces a new ‘public benefit fund’ to commit 5% of its stocks: What we know
items.blurb: Anthropic plans to commit 5% of its shares to a public benefit fund, subject to stockholder approval, with scope to expand the stake as its value grows. Elon Musk suggested giving shares directly to the public. The announcement comes ahead of the AI firm’s IPO, reportedly scheduled for November.
items.text: Artificial intelligence (AI) firm Anthropic on Sunday (local time) announced that it will commit roughly five per cent of its shares to a new "public benefit" fund, whose value could rise alongside the company’s share price. The shares will go to the "Anthropic Public Benefit Fund", a new entity within the company, the AI firm announced in a blog post. Anthropic added, "Today, we’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new entity with a structure that increases the stake as the company grows. Subject to stockholder approval, 5% of Anthropic’s shares will be committed today, with an additional 2% added at the board’s discretion for every 50% increase in the company’s value above a set baseline." It also said the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund will have greater flexibility and scale, allowing the AI firm to pursue its mission through new approaches, including substantial donations to traditional nonprofits or direct payments to selected groups. items.blurb: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex.
items.text: The Indian government is engaging in discussions about measuring Scope 3 emissions for exporters. This consideration arises as trade partners impose tighter green requirements globally. Current frameworks focus on direct emissions and exclude indirect ones, making compliance more complex. As a result, industries, especially MSMEs, may face compliance burdens if new requirements are implemented. Ultimately, the aim is to ensure that Indian exporters remain competitive in international markets. items.headline: Microsoft pulls out of UK's largest AI data centre
items.blurb: Tech firm Nscale says it is still committed to building the site in Essex.
items.text: A tech company has said it still plans to build the UK's largest AI data centre despite Microsoft pulling out of the project. Nscale announced last year it had pledged £2bn to build and open a pioneering facility in Loughton , Essex. However, the BBC understands that Microsoft, which said it would fund a supercomputer at the site, has terminated its involvement. A spokesperson for Nscale said it was exploring alternative power sources and its relationship with Microsoft remained strong for their other projects together overseas. Microsoft declined to comment. "We remain committed to both the Loughton project and the UK and we are exploring alternative power sources for the site, in addition to other expansion sites in the UK," Nscale said. The data centre was due to receive its power supply at the end of the year. But as first reported by the Telegraph on Sunday , external , Nscale has been told this will not happen until the 2030s. items.text: Mumbai: Focus Prism, a Coimbatore-based food services platform that raised ₹ 145 crore from OAKS Asset Management last month, has acquired FoodExo Chennai Pvt. Ltd, underscoring the consolidation of assets in a niche segment and growing institutionalization in a sector currently dominated by global players. Through the capital infusion, OAKS has taken a significant minority stake in Focus Prism. While the bulk of the proceeds from the fundraise financed the acquisition, Focus Prism also reserved a portion of the capital for other growth plans, Vivek Anand, managing director and founder of OAKS, told Mint . The acquisition was about ₹ 150 crore in size and was a mix of stock and cash, he added. Led by founder and managing director Ganesh Panchanathan, Chennai-based FoodExo is a leading corporate catering company serving various industries. Established in 2011, it began with 60 employees serving 1,000 people and has scaled up to more and 2,000 employees serving 150,000 meals per day as of 2025. The company also swung to a net profit of Rs 63.42 crore, steered by the sale of its stake in FreshBus and Rs 22 crore in other income. The Gurugram-based company’s operating revenue increased 13% year-on-year to Rs 321 crore in Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 284 crore in Q2 FY26, according to its unaudited financial results sourced from the National Stock Exchange. Train bookings remained the largest contributor to the company's operating revenue, spiking 16.4% year-on-year to Rs 149.1 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 128.1 crore in the corresponding quarter last year. Bus revenue grew 23.8% to Rs 81 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 65.4 crore, whereas revenue from flight bookings declined 7.5% to Rs 82.7 crore in Q2FY27 from Rs 89.4 crore. items.text: Noni Madueke may not have the starting role he wants at Arsenal, but his winning goal against Nottingham Forest showed why he is one of Mikel Arteta's valued "finishers". The England international scored in the second half to earn Arsenal a 1–0 result and three valuable points towards their defence of the Premier League title. Madueke has started just one top-flight game this season, the 2–1 win over Leeds that came eight days prior to their victory over Oliver Glasner's Forest on Sunday. Arsenal 's summer was dominated by talk of their search for an elite forward, with the left wing one of the positions identified. But after unsuccessful pursuits of superstar players such as Vinicius Jr and Julian Alvarez, the only new addition in that position was Christos Tzolis, the winger brought in to replace the outgoing Leandro Trossard. Tzolis has started the season well and has been the first-choice winger for Arteta, meaning that Madueke and Eberechi Eze have had to be content with the majority of their minutes coming from the bench or in the Carabao Cup.

METR, a nonprofit that has worked with leading labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta, now has a team embedded in the Claude maker’s office with access to its hardware and internal systems. A greater role for third-party evaluators is among the main concrete steps the labs have proposed in response to rising concern about the dangers more capable AI systems could pose to the economy, cyber security and humanity at large. items.text: Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Watch as senior AI reporter James O'Donnell interviews King about his work, being named one of MIT Technology Review's Innovators Under 35 and new ways of seeing biology. Speakers : James O'Donnell , AI Reporter, and Samuel King , Bioengineering PhD Candidate, Stanford University/Arc Institute Ten years after AlphaGo’s match against Go champion Lee Sedol, today’s AI still isn’t tapping into the machinery that made that win possible. AI agents are not yet creative enough to carry out genuinely innovative open-ended AI research, it seems. Breathless claims about AGI and new capabilities fall apart pretty quickly under scrutiny. The underlying models had been rewarded for cheating and communicating with each other, a new OpenAI report finds.

items.headline: OpenAI models hacked a crypto wallet and breached more websites
items.blurb: The actions could have resulted in criminal charges had humans been behind the keyboard.
items.text: OpenAI said internal models hacked two more websites, bypassed company-imposed browsing restrictions, and used exposed credentials to draw cryptocurrency from a wallet it couldn’t otherwise access, in the latest installment of disclosures of its agents performing unethical and likely illegal acts. The company on Thursday issued reports of four new incidents, all of which occurred in June. They come after the company revealed in July that internal test agents exploited a zero-day vulnerability in a tool designed to restrict their access to the Internet. They then broke into the network of AI tool provider Hugging Face. The agents took that illegal action to steal answers to a hacking test that weren’t available when completing the tasks on their own. The incident—which likely would have resulted in criminal charges had they been performed directly by a person—has further heightened concerns that widespread AI use could have harmful effects on an unprecedented scale.
